answer: An agent economy can require each new identity to lock a scarce, slashable stake before it can post jobs or claim payouts. Contracts release the stake only after a cooling-off period and penalize identities that coordinate duplicate claims or fail audited work; linked evidence can trigger forfeiture. This does not prove one person has one identity, but it makes Sybil scale costly: an attacker must tie up capital across identities and risks losing it. Whether the market is an oasis, mesa, or ocean, the same cost applies.
